verses.1: And Bileam saw that it was good in the eyes of Jehovah to bless Israel. He did not go out to see the snakes once again. Instead, he turned his face towards the sea.
verses.2: And Bileam raised his eyes and saw that Israel was under his control. Then a spirit of God rested upon him.
verses.3: And he raised his hand and said, “Let there be a great noise in Bilam’s land. And let there be a great noise as well in the valley.”
verses.4: May those who hear the words of the Lord, who sees all things that will happen, be able to see clearly and understand everything.
verses.5: What good is your dwelling place, Jacob, compared to the dwellings of Israel!
verses.6: The streams are like gardens along the rivers. The LORD has planted them like trees along the seas.
verses.7: Water will pour down from Daliyav, and its seeds will be scattered in many waters. It will also destroy the throne of the king. His queen will be taken away.
verses.8: They brought him out of Egypt, as if he were a fugitive. The nations of Egypt will eat him up; their own people will destroy him. Half of them will be destroyed.
verses.9: He lay down like a donkey and a dog. Who will create us again, O Lord? Blessed and exalted be Your name.
verses.10: And Balak struck his hands together and said to Bileam, “Come here! I call upon you. Now, bless me three times.”
verses.11: And now, as you depart for your place, I said, “I will protect you.” But now, behold, Jehovah has withdrawn you from your protection.
verses.12: And Bilam said to Balak, “Have you not also sent your servants to me with these words?”
verses.13: If I were given wealth in my house, with gold and silver, it would still not be enough for me to do good or evil according to what Jehovah has commanded me. Jehovah will speak through those who speak.
verses.14: And now, I go back to my people to report your warning about what this people will do to your people in the days to come.
verses.15: And he raised his hand and said, “Let there be light in the darkness. And let the morning come upon us.”
verses.16: May he listen to the words of God and understand His wisdom. Then, those who are doomed will be destroyed, and their secrets will be revealed to everyone’s eyes.
verses.17: Let us see; do not now be deceived. Let us not follow the path taken by Jacob. Let the tribes of Israel rise up, and let them cross over the borders of Moab. May all the children of Seth be destroyed.
verses.18: And Adam would inherit it. And Adam’s descendants would also inherit it. And Israel would be able to live there.
verses.19: And Yaakov would descend from Mount Sinai, and he would take away the remains of the city with him.
verses.20: And he saw Amalek, and he raised his sword. He said, “Amalek will be destroyed first, and then all his people will be destroyed.”
verses.21: And he saw the pot, and he took it up. He said, “Eitan, you shall sit here, and put your pot in the basket.”
verses.22: For if there is any hope of survival, then Ashur will be able to restore you to your former state.
verses.23: And he raised his hand and said, “Oh, who will survive from this place?”
verses.24: And they were destroyed by hands of the sword; Ashur and Enlil also were destroyed. And he too was destroyed.
verses.25: And he arose from Gilgal, went away, and returned to his place. And also, Balak went on his way.
